subject: physics
pattern: This is a short chapter that normally fetches 4-6 marks: one 1-mark (displacement current, speed of EM waves, uses of a region of the spectrum), one 2-mark or 3-mark question on properties or sources and uses of EM waves, and an occasional numerical on $B_0 = E_0/c$ or on wavelength and frequency. Examiners expect Maxwell's displacement current idea, the formula $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}$ and a clear table or list of the spectrum with one use each.

questions.answer: The current that arises due to a time-varying electric field (changing electric flux) in a region, such as between the plates of a charging capacitor, is called displacement current. It is given by $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, where $\Phi_E$ is the electric flux. It was introduced by Maxwell to make Ampere's circuital law consistent.

questions.q: Write the expression for the speed of electromagnetic waves in free space in terms of $\mu_0$ and $\epsilon_0$.
questions.answer: $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$. Substituting $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T m A$^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$ N$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$ gives $c \approx 3\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Name the part of the electromagnetic spectrum used in RADAR systems and in microwave ovens.
questions.answer: Microwaves. Their short wavelength (about 1 mm to 0.1 m) allows them to be beamed in a particular direction in RADAR, and their frequency matches the natural frequency of water molecules, so they heat food in microwave ovens.

questions.q: Mention any four characteristics of electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer:
1. EM waves are produced by accelerated charges and need no material medium; they travel in vacuum with speed $c = 3\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$.
2. They are transverse: the electric field $\vec E$ and magnetic field $\vec B$ are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.
3. $E$ and $B$ oscillate in phase, and $E_0/B_0 = c$.
4. They are not deflected by electric or magnetic fields, and they carry energy and momentum.

questions.q: Mention two uses each of infrared waves and ultraviolet waves.
questions.answer:
Infrared waves: (i) used in physical therapy to treat muscular strain; (ii) used in remote controls of TVs and in night-vision / greenhouse effect applications (they keep the Earth warm).
Ultraviolet waves: (i) used in LASIK eye surgery; (ii) used to sterilise water purifiers and surgical instruments, and in detecting forged documents.

questions.q: The electric field amplitude of an electromagnetic wave in free space is $E_0 = 18$ V m$^{-1}$. Calculate the amplitude of the magnetic field. ($c = 3\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$)
Why are electromagnetic waves not deflected by electric and magnetic fields?
questions.answer: Electromagnetic waves are made of oscillating electric and magnetic fields and carry no electric charge. An electric or magnetic field can exert a force only on a charged particle (or a current), so the neutral EM wave is not deflected by them.

questions.q: What was the inconsistency in Ampere's circuital law while charging a capacitor? How did Maxwell remove it? Write the modified law.
questions.answer:
While a capacitor charges, current $I$ flows in the wires but none flows across the gap between the plates. Taking a loop around the wire, Ampere's law gives $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 I$ for a flat surface cutting the wire, but zero for a bulging surface passing between the plates. This is a contradiction.
Maxwell proposed that a changing electric flux between the plates acts as a current, the displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0\, d\Phi_E/dt$. The corrected Ampere-Maxwell law is
$\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 (I_c + I_d) = \mu_0 I_c + \mu_0\epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 25 MHz travels in free space along the x-direction. At a particular point and time, $\vec E = 6.3$ V m$^{-1}$ along the y-direction. Find the magnitude and direction of $\vec B$ at that point. Also find the wavelength.
questions.answer:
$B = \dfrac{E}{c} = \dfrac{6.3}{3\times10^{8}} = 2.1\times10^{-8}$ T.
Since $\vec E \times \vec B$ must point along the direction of propagation (+x), and $\vec E$ is along +y, $\vec B$ is along the +z direction.
Wavelength: $\lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3\times10^{8}}{25\times10^{6}} = 12$ m.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic radiations that have (i) the longest wavelength, (ii) the highest frequency and (iii) are produced by the de-excitation of nuclei. Give one use of each.
questions.answer:
(i) Radio waves have the longest wavelength (above about 0.1 m); used in radio and television communication.
(ii) Gamma rays have the highest frequency (shortest wavelength, below about $10^{-12}$ m); used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells.
(iii) Gamma rays are emitted by excited nuclei during radioactive decay (de-excitation); they are also used to study nuclear structure and sterilise medical equipment.

questions.q: Write the source and one use of each of the following: (i) radio waves, (ii) microwaves, (iii) X-rays.
questions.answer:
(i) Radio waves: produced by accelerated charges in conducting wires (oscillating circuits); used in radio and TV broadcasting.
(ii) Microwaves: produced by special vacuum tubes such as klystron and magnetron; used in RADAR, mobile communication and microwave ovens.
(iii) X-rays: produced when high-energy electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal target (or by inner-shell electron transitions); used in medical diagnosis (to see fractures) and airport security.

questions.q: State Maxwell's four equations in integral form and mention the physical meaning of each.
questions.answer:
1. Gauss's law for electricity: $\oint \vec E\cdot d\vec A = \dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}$ - electric flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by $\epsilon_0$; charges are sources of electric field.
2. Gauss's law for magnetism: $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec A = 0$ - there are no magnetic monopoles; magnetic field lines are closed.
3. Faraday's law: $\oint \vec E\cdot d\vec l = -\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt}$ - a changing magnetic flux induces an electric field.
4. Ampere-Maxwell law: $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0 I + \mu_0\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ - a current and a changing electric flux produce a magnetic field.
Together they predict EM waves travelling with $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}$.

questions.q: Name the different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength, giving the approximate wavelength range, source and one use of any five of them.
questions.answer:
In order of increasing wavelength: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio waves.
- Gamma rays ($<10^{-12}$ m): radioactive nuclei; radiotherapy.
- X-rays ($10^{-8}$ to $10^{-13}$ m): sudden stopping of fast electrons; medical imaging.
- Ultraviolet ($4\times10^{-7}$ to $6\times10^{-10}$ m): Sun, mercury lamp; LASIK, sterilisation.
- Visible ($7\times10^{-7}$ to $4\times10^{-7}$ m): hot bodies, lamps; vision.
- Infrared ($10^{-3}$ to $7\times10^{-7}$ m): hot bodies, molecular vibrations; physical therapy, remote controls.
- Microwaves (1 mm to 0.1 m): klystron, magnetron; RADAR, ovens.
- Radio waves (above 0.1 m): accelerated charges in circuits; broadcasting.
